en: The Hymn of Praise to Śrī Datta (Śrī Dattastavastotra)
By the mere remembrance of whom, [the afflictions of] bhūtas, pretas, piśācas, and the like [are dispelled].
They flee from afar; I bow to that Dattātreya. || 1 ||
Through the remembrance of which, wretchedness, sin, and suffering are destroyed.
I bow to that Dattātreya, who removes fear, seizure, and evil dreams. || 2 ||
Ringworm, pustules, leprosy, and the like, as well as great pestilence and cholera.
Other diseases as well perish; I bow to that Dattātreya. || 3 ||
Diseases arising from specific places and times are also contagious.
I bow to that Dattātreya, by the mere remembrance of whom [all afflictions] are stilled.
For embodied beings afflicted by poison from being bitten by snakes or scorpions.
I bow to that Dattātreya, who indeed swiftly bestows peace. || 5 ||
It pacifies the three kinds of portents and destroys various signs of impending death.
I bow to that Dattātreya, who indeed destroys cruelty and fear.
By whose mere recitation the application of spells, mantras, and the like performed by others is rendered ineffective.
The afflictions caused by the gods perish; I bow down to that Dattātreya.
By the mere recollection of which, that which has been lost or gone is immediately recovered.
I bow to that Dattātreya, who is the Lord and the protector from all sides.
This is the praise of Datta, the bestower of victory, gain, fame, and desire.
One who recites this [hymn] which bestows both worldly enjoyment and liberation shall become beloved by the Giver (Śiva). || 9 ||
Thus ends the Dattastava-stotra composed by Śrī Vāsudevānanda Sarasvatī.
